title: Ops dashboards: filters + drilldowns for incident_type and owner (avoid misinterpretation for Unknown/Unclassified)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Reliability Program — Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
## Context
We’re adding a required incident taxonomy (incident_type + subtype) and ownership mapping to incident tooling and reporting. Console/ops dashboards need a consistent way to:
- Filter incident analytics by incident_type/subtype and owner
- Drill down without exploding cardinality or creating confusing UI
- Prevent incorrect conclusions when data is incomplete (Unknown/Unclassified)

This ticket defines the filter UX + drilldown patterns for the new **Incident Taxonomy dashboards** in Console (ops-only initially), aligned with the Confluence dashboard spec and observability cardinality constraints.

Related:
- Confluence spec: `sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/incident-taxonomy-dashboards-spec.json`
- Remediation SLAs: `ENG-4829` / `PM-912`
- Console exposure: `PM-913`

## Goals
1) Make it fast for on-call + SRE to answer: “What’s breaking? Who owns it? Is this recurring?”
2) Ensure filters are usable during live incidents (low friction, defaults that match how ICs think).
3) Make Unknown/Unclassified visible and correctly interpreted (data quality, not a category of incidents).
4) Provide a consistent interaction model that can be reused across multiple dashboard panels.

## Non-goals
- Defining taxonomy names/definitions (handled in taxonomy v1 doc + incident-bot)
- Building the dashboards (ENG-4828)
- Building owner mapping config (ENG-4825)

## Primary users / modes
- **SRE / Incident Commander:** triage and trend review; wants quick filters + confidence in data.
- **Infra/Fleet, Routing, Runtime, Observability on-call:** needs owner + subtype drilldowns.
- **Support/CS (view-only):** needs simplified, safe views; avoid implying root cause.

## Information architecture (dashboards + common filter bar)
All incident taxonomy dashboards share a **global filter bar** at top:
- Time range (default: last 7d)
- Tier (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) — default: All, but allow saved views
- Severity (Sev0/Sev1/Sev2/Sev3) — default: Sev0–Sev2
- Incident Type (top-level) — multi-select
- Subtype — dependent multi-select (enabled when exactly 1 type selected)
- Owner (Primary owner team) — multi-select
- Region (optional, collapsible) — single/multi (to match how incidents are triaged)

Design principle: **make “type → subtype” hierarchical in UI**, but avoid rendering the full tree unless requested.

## Filter interaction details
### 1) Incident Type (multi-select)
- Control: searchable multi-select dropdown with pinned “Top types (last 30d)” section.
- Values: allowlist only (matches incident-bot + metrics allowlist).
- Display: show label + short definition in hover tooltip (1 line) to reduce ambiguity.

### 2) Subtype (dependent)
- Default state: disabled with helper text “Select 1 incident type to choose subtypes”.
- When enabled: multi-select dropdown showing subtypes for that selected type.
- Rationale: prevents confusing “mixed subtype sets” that don’t share semantics.

### 3) Owner (primary owner)
- Control: searchable multi-select.
- Source of truth: owner resolved from control-plane mapping (versioned).
- Note: a banner appears if “Owner mapping version changed in selected time range” (see Data trust section).

### 4) Severity + Tier defaults (anti-footgun)
- Severity default: Sev0–Sev2 to focus on customer-impacting/high urgency; include Sev3 via toggle.
- Tier default: All, but we ship saved views:
  - “Hosted — On-call”
  - “Dedicated — On-call”
  - “Private — On-call”

### 5) URL state + shareability
- All filter values are encoded into URL query params so links in Slack/incident-bot are stable.
- “Copy link” action in filter bar.

## Drilldown patterns
### A) Click-to-filter from charts
- Clicking a chart segment (e.g., bar for Routing owner) updates the filter bar and refreshes all panels.
- A “breadcrumb chip row” appears under the filter bar to show implicit filters created by clicks.

### B) Detail drawer for a segment
When clicking a panel header action “View details”, open a right-side drawer:
- Shows top incidents in that segment (title, start time, duration, severity, tier)
- Shows classification completeness for that segment
- Includes links to incident channel / postmortem (where available)

This avoids forcing users into a separate page while preserving context.

## Unknown / Unclassified handling (prevent misinterpretation)
We need to distinguish three states:
1) **Unknown (not yet classified):** incident exists but no incident_type set yet (usually early in incident).
2) **Unclassified (legacy/backfill gap):** incident predates enforcement or couldn’t be inferred with confidence.
3) **Other / Not in allowlist:** should not exist in v1 metrics labeling; if it does, treat as data bug.

### UI representation rules
- Unknown/Unclassified are **not grouped into the taxonomy list**. They appear as a separate “Data quality” bucket.
- Default behavior: include Unknown/Unclassified in totals, but visually annotate panels:
  - Panels that include type breakdown show an extra bar/row labeled “Data quality: Unknown/Unclassified”.
  - That label is gray + dotted pattern (distinct from incident categories).
- Global filter bar includes a toggle:
  - **Include data quality buckets** (default ON)
  - When OFF, totals and charts recompute excluding Unknown/Unclassified; a warning note appears “Totals exclude unclassified incidents”.

### Data trust banner
At top of dashboard (below filter bar), show a banner when either condition is true:
- Unknown/Unclassified > 10% of incidents in selected time range, OR
- A “type enforcement rollout start date” overlaps selected range

Banner copy (draft):
- “Classification coverage is 84% for this view. Some panels include ‘Unknown/Unclassified’ incidents. Learn more.”
- “Learn more” links to incident classification policy + how to backfill.

### Tooltip language guidelines
- Avoid wording that implies root cause. Use: “Incident type classification (operational category)” not “Cause”.
- Owner label: “Primary on-call owner” (not “Responsible team for root cause”).

## Accessibility + performance constraints
- Dropdowns must support keyboard navigation + typeahead.
- Multi-select chips should collapse after 3 selections into “+N more” to avoid taking over the header.
- Filters should not require loading the entire taxonomy tree client-side; subtype options can be fetched on demand for selected type.

## Console permissions / CS safety
- Ops dashboard page is internal; CS view will likely be read-only.
- In CS-safe mode (future):
  - Hide “Data quality buckets” toggle (kept ON)
  - Replace owner with “Owning engineering area” (broader) if needed
  - Lock severity to Sev0–Sev2

## Deliverables
- Figma exploration: filter bar, dropdown behaviors, detail drawer, data trust banner
- Spec notes for implementation (ENG-4828 / PM-913): query params, empty states, label rules for Unknown/Unclassified

Figma link (internal): https://figma.redwoodinference.com/file/ConsoleOps-IncidentTaxonomy-Filters-DES-441

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Filter bar spec covers: time range, tier, severity, type/subtype hierarchy, owner
- [x] Unknown vs Unclassified treatment is explicit and cannot be mistaken for a category
- [x] Click-to-filter + drawer drilldown patterns documented
- [x] Implementation notes for URL/query params and defaults included

## Open questions (resolved here unless noted)
- Q: Should subtype be selectable when multiple types selected?
  - A: No (v1). Too confusing; revisit after usage.
- Q: Should we default to excluding Unknown/Unclassified?
  - A: No. Keep included to avoid hiding data quality problems; add banner + toggle.
- Q: What’s the threshold for showing the banner?
  - A: 10% coverage gap (tunable; confirm with SRE after week 1 of rollout).
comments: 2025-12-20 — Talia Benson: Creating this to unblock ENG-4828. Key risk is misinterpretation of Unknown/Unclassified; please be opinionated and explicit in UI.

2025-12-23 — Allison Grant: +1 on separating data quality buckets from taxonomy. Also please avoid multi-level filters that allow arbitrary combinations; keep subtype dependent on 1 type selection (cardinality + UX).

2025-12-27 — Sergio Costa: Drafted filter bar variants. Proposal: global filters at top + click-to-filter from charts. Subtype disabled until exactly 1 type selected. Added URL query params to make Slack links stable.

2026-01-03 — Rafael Mendes: Looks good. Ask: make the banner show classification coverage % and link to policy. We want Unknown to be treated as “during-incident incomplete info”, Unclassified as “legacy/backfill gap.”

2026-01-06 — Dev Patel: From Support perspective: wording should avoid implying root cause. Owner should read as “Primary on-call owner” not “Responsible.” Also ensure CS-safe views don’t encourage over-sharing internal details.

2026-01-08 — Sergio Costa: Updated spec: dotted pattern/gray styling for data quality segments; added toggle copy and warning state when excluding Unknown/Unclassified. Linked Figma and added implementation notes for dependent subtype dropdown.
2026-01-10 — Talia Benson: Marking Done. Next: Sergio to paste key implementation notes into ENG-4828 and PM-913, especially the data trust banner + query param requirements.
